messages:
sylvie: New hire hit a puzzler: `redwoodctl auth login` prints "Authenticated" but `redwoodctl samples run` errors with "rpc: unauthenticated". They had both Homebrew and a manual tarball install. Turns out their zsh had an autocompletion shim that pointed `redwoodctl` to /usr/local/bin while brew put it in /opt/homebrew/bin. Binary versions differ and each looked at different config locations.

mark: Oof. Multiple installs + shell shims is a classic. Can you get `which -a redwoodctl` and `redwoodctl --version` for each path? Also `echo $PATH` and check for completion functions in ~/.zshrc that wrap commands.

sylvie: repro I pasted to them:
1) tarball install -> /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl v2.2.0 that uses legacy ~/.redwood
2) brew install -> /opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl v2.4.1 that prefers XDG
3) zsh completion/alias had `compdef _redwoodctl redwoodctl` and path order favors /usr/local/bin
Result: interactive login touched XDG (brew binary) but samples runner invoked the other binary which looked in ~/.redwood -> unauthenticated. `which -a` shows both.

toni: thanks Sylvie. Two immediate fixes: a) onboarding doc should warn about multiple installs and show `which -a` check; b) CLI should print a clear hint when unauthenticated like: "Multiple redwoodctl binaries detected: run `which -a redwoodctl` to ensure you are using the same binary for auth and serve." Could also detect if there are multiple binaries with different versions and warn on startup.

mark: raising an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/1255 "detect multiple installations and warn; unify config discovery across installs". Proposed changes: (1) runtime prints a startup banner in --verbose that shows resolved binary path and config dir; (2) unauthenticated errors suggest `which -a` and `REDWOOD_CONFIG_DIR` workarounds; (3) add a `redwoodctl self-check` that verifies install consistency (single binary in PATH, autocompletion matches).

devex-bot: devex checklist: add a short section to onboarding about "one true redwoodctl" with commands to remove stale installs, update PATH, and how to uninstall tarball installs. Also add a CI test that runs `which -a` in a container with two binaries to ensure the warning triggers.

ci-bot: note: changing unauthenticated text may affect CLI-based tests that assert exact error strings. Add migration note and update tests. Also add an e2e that performs auth with one binary and runs samples with a different one to make sure the warning appears.

sylvie: temporary workaround: symlink the brew binary into /usr/local/bin or remove the old tarball. New hire fixed it by removing /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl and now both commands behave. I'll paste the repro and minimal shell outputs into the GH issue. :thumbsup:
